# Digital Human Koubo · AI 数字人口播 **One photo + one sentence → a finished talking-head video with a digital human.** Script, lip-synced AI presenter, voice clean-up, captions, and pro-YouTuber-style packaging — fully automated by your AI agent. **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-black.svg)](LICENSE) ![Agent Skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent%20Skill-SKILL.md-orange) [![Renoise MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/video-Renoise%20MCP-ff7a1a)](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official) ![Remotion](https://img.shields.io/badge/edit-Remotion%204-0b84f3)
> This 27-second livestream ad has no real presenter. Face, voice, studio, captions and the price animation are all AI. > The only input was one sentence: *"Use this digital human to make a 30-second livestream ad for the WorkBuddy course — 10 lessons, ¥99, was ¥999."* > Total cost: **482 [Renoise](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official) credits**. --- ## Demos Click a GIF (or "Watch") to play the full video. Every demo below was produced with this repo. | | | | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | | **Livestream sales ad** · 9:16 · 27 s

[▶ Watch](https://github.com/andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo/releases/download/v1.0.0/xiaolin-style-explainer.mp4) |

Packaging component gallery · 48 components · 2:40 · ▶ Watch
> All presenters in the demos are AI digital humans and every video is labelled "内容由 AI 数字人演绎" (performed by an AI digital human). The male presenter is the author's own digital twin, made from his own photo. --- ## What it does - **Digital human from one photo** — a fixed presenter (face, outfit, voice description, prompt template) stored in `persona.json`, so every video is the same person. Composite her into any scene (livestream studio, shop, classroom, Kyoto street) with GPT Image first, then make her talk. - **Lip-synced talking clips** — the script is split into ≤ 15-second segments and generated with **Grok Video 1.5** through **[Renoise MCP](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official)**. Other models (Wan 3.0, OmniHuman for your own recording) are documented. - **Cost gate** — the agent always quotes *segments · seconds · credits · balance* first and waits for your "yes". It generates segment 1 for you to check before batching the rest. - **Quality control** — every segment is transcribed with whisper and compared with the script, and 4 frames per segment are inspected (Grok sometimes burns subtitles into the picture; those segments get re-shot). - **Voice unification** — 1/3-octave spectral matching, de-essing, one shared small-room reverb and loudness normalisation, so 30 separately-generated clips sound like one recording (sibilance spread 13.2 dB → 5.9 dB in our tests). - **5 editing styles, chosen for your content** — the agent diagnoses your content, recommends 2 styles with preview images and asks you everything in one go (style · ratio & length · caption intensity · presenter). - **48 packaging components** — measured frame-by-frame from 25 videos by top creators (MrBeast, Mark Rober, Ryan Trahan, MKBHD, MediaStorm/影视飓风, 何同学, Johnny Harris, Vox, Kurzgesagt, 回形针, 半佛仙人, 差评, 毕导). Each style has a default packaging recipe; add or remove techniques by just asking. - **Text behind the presenter** — big words / numbers between the background and the person (macOS Vision person segmentation → transparent video → 3-layer composite). - **Multi-language** — English, Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, Arabic tested (whisper back-check 94–100 %). - **Works with your agent** — a standard `SKILL.md` Agent Skill plus scripts; any agent that can load skills, connect a remote MCP server and run local commands can drive it. ## How it works ``` your content ──► 0. setup check (Renoise MCP / ffmpeg / whisper — skip what you already have) 1. diagnose content → recommend 2 of 5 styles → ask once → brief.json 2. script.json (≤15 s per segment, ~5.4 Chinese chars/s) 3. quote credits → wait for "yes" → generate segment 1 → you check → batch 4. range-download (CDN-safe) → whisper back-check → frame check 5. voice unification (spectral match + de-ess + shared room) 6. word-level timeline (tl.json) 7. edit in Remotion: style template + default packaging (+ your requests) 8. render → check mid-transition frames → loudness (-14 / -16 LUFS) ```

--- ## Supported agents The skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` (the open Agent Skills format) plus Python / shell / Remotion scripts. To run the **whole** pipeline an agent needs three things: 1. **Load Agent Skills** (a skills folder or skill upload), 2. **Connect a remote MCP server** (Renoise — streamable HTTP, browser login, no API key), 3. **Run commands on your computer** (ffmpeg, Python, Node — for downloading, QA and editing). | Agent | Skills | Renoise MCP | Local commands | Status | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | `~/.claude/skills/` | `/plugin` (below) | ✅ | ✅ Tested — this repo was built with it | | **Codex** (CLI / desktop) | `~/.codex/skills/` | `codex mcp add` | ✅ | ✅ Expected to work (same scripts) | | **OpenClaw** | skills folder per OpenClaw docs | `openclaw plugins install` | ✅ | ⚙️ Should work | | **WorkBuddy** | Skills → import the folder / zip | Connectors → add custom MCP | ✅ desktop agent | ⚙️ Should work — menu names may differ by version | | **豆包 (Doubao)** · **千问办公 (Qwen Office)** · **纳米Work (NamiWork)** and other agent products | import if the product supports Agent Skills | add as a custom / remote MCP server if supported | needed for editing | ⚙️ Works if the product supports the 3 requirements above; check its docs | | **Claude desktop / claude.ai** | upload the skill zip in Settings | Connectors → Add custom connector | ⚠️ sandbox only | Script writing, scene design, generation & quoting work; local editing needs a shell agent | > If your agent can only do MCP + chat (no local commands), you can still use it to **plan, quote and generate** the clips through Renoise; then run the editing steps with Claude Code / Codex, or by hand with the commands in [`SKILL.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/SKILL.md). --- ## Installation ### 1 · Get the code ```bash git clone https://github.com/andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo.git cd digital-human-koubo ``` ### 2 · Install the two skills into your agent The repo contains two skills: `digital-human-koubo` (main) and `finance-explainer` (the engine for Style A, the finance / tech explainer). **Claude Code** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -R skills/digital-human-koubo skills/finance-explainer ~/.claude/skills/ ``` **Codex** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.codex/skills && cp -R skills/digital-human-koubo skills/finance-explainer ~/.codex/skills/ ``` **WorkBuddy / OpenClaw / other agents** — zip the two folders and import them in the product's *Skills* page, or copy them into its skills directory (see the product's docs): ```bash cd skills && zip -r ../digital-human-skills.zip digital-human-koubo finance-explainer && cd .. ``` ### 3 · Connect Renoise MCP (AI video / image generation) Create an account at **[renoise.ai](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official)** first. Login is in the browser — you never paste an API key. | Agent | How | |---|---| | Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add ArcoCodes/renoise-plugins-official` then `/plugin install renoise@renoise-plugins-official` | | Codex | `codex mcp add renoise --url https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` then `codex mcp login renoise` | | OpenClaw | `openclaw plugins install renoise --marketplace ArcoCodes/renoise-plugins-official` | | Claude desktop / claude.ai | Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector** → name `Renoise`, URL `https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` | | WorkBuddy, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, 豆包, 千问, 纳米Work, … | add a remote MCP server with URL `https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp` (typical config: `{"mcpServers":{"renoise":{"url":"https://renoise.ai/api/public/mcp"}}}`) | Latest official instructions: **[renoise.ai/plugin](https://renoise.ai/plugin)**. Check it worked by asking your agent: *"查一下我的 Renoise 余额 / check my Renoise balance."* ### 4 · Local tools (for downloading, QA and editing) | Tool | macOS | Windows | Linux | |---|---|---|---| | ffmpeg | `brew install ffmpeg` | `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` | `sudo apt install ffmpeg` | | Python 3 + numpy + Pillow | `brew install python` then `python3 -m pip install numpy pillow` | `winget install Python.Python.3.12` | `sudo apt install python3-pip` | | Node.js 18+ (Remotion) | `brew install node` | `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` | `nvm install --lts` | | whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli`) | `brew install whisper-cpp` | [Releases](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/releases) | build from [source](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp) | | whisper model | [`ggml-medium-q5_0.bin`](https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-medium-q5_0.bin) → `~/models/` (or `export WHISPER_MODEL=/path/to/model.bin`) | same | same | One-command check — it skips what you have and lists install options for what's missing: ```bash bash ~/.claude/skills/digital-human-koubo/scripts/doctor.sh ``` The **text-behind-presenter** effect uses Apple Vision and needs **macOS**; everything else is cross-platform. ### 5 · Sound effects & placeholder music The repo ships **no third-party audio**. Generate an original set of 30 sound effects and a placeholder background track (pure code, no copyright): ```bash python3 ~/.claude/skills/digital-human-koubo/scripts/make_assets.py ``` `new_edit.sh` also runs this automatically for every new project. For a better soundtrack, drop any track you have the rights to at `/public/music/bgm.mp3`. ### 6 · (Optional) Xiaomi MiMo TTS — designed or cloned voices The default voice is Grok's native voice (best lip-sync). For a designed voice, your own cloned voice, or narration-only videos, the skill uses **Xiaomi MiMo TTS**: 1. Register at **[platform.xiaomimimo.com](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/)** and create an API key. At the time of writing Xiaomi offered the TTS models free for a limited time — check the site for current pricing. 2. Put the key in an environment variable, or in `~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env`: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.config/ai-teardown && cat > ~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env <<'EOF' MIMO_API_KEY=your-key-here MIMO_BASE_URL=https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1 EOF chmod 600 ~/.config/ai-teardown/mimo.env ``` 3. Only clone **your own** voice or a voice you have explicit permission to use. > Note: Grok generates lip movement from its own voice. Swapping in a different voice afterwards leaves ~100 ms lip offset (fine in picture-in-picture, visible in full-screen close-ups). For your own recording with exact lip-sync, use an audio-driven model such as OmniHuman (documented in the skill). --- ## Quick start Talk to your agent in plain language: ```text 用我的数字人 Skill 讲这段：……（paste your content） Use my digital human skill to make a 30-second livestream ad: WorkBuddy course, 10 lessons, ¥99 (was ¥999). Make a 3-minute explainer about why Silicon Valley Bank collapsed, Xiaolin-style. Add a map route when she mentions these countries. / Put "¥99" behind her. / Add a teaser cold open. 把包装组件图鉴发我看看 (show me the packaging gallery) ``` What happens next: 1. Setup check — anything already installed is skipped. 2. A one-line diagnosis + 2 recommended styles with preview images, and one round of questions. 3. Script + scene design + **credit quote** → you approve → segment 1 → you approve → the rest. 4. QA, voice clean-up, editing with the style's default packaging → the finished MP4. --- ## Make your own digital human 1. Pick a photo: frontal face, even light, hair off the face, mouth closed. **Only your own photo or one you have permission to use.** 2. Ask the agent to generate a 4-view sheet (front, both sides, back) — GPT Image 2.5, 2k, ~23 credits — so the face stays the same from every angle. 3. Compare models with the same image and line (Grok Video 1.5 vs Wan 3.0, 8 s each) and pick one. 4. Upload the reference to Renoise and put its `material:` into `skills/digital-human-koubo/persona.json` (`renoise.reference_material`, or `other_hosts.me` for a second presenter). Details: [`references/new-avatar.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/new-avatar.md). The `material:` IDs in this repo belong to the author's account and won't work on yours — that's expected.

--- ## Five editing styles

| Style | Ratio | Length | Best for | Template | |---|---|---|---|---| | **A** Finance / tech explainer (Xiaolin-style structure) | 16:9 | 3–20 min | events, data, "why…" | `finance-explainer` engine | | **B** Influencer talking head with animated captions | 9:16 | 30–120 s | product picks, sales, opinions | `templates/huazi-916` (data-driven) | | **C** Launch breakdown | 16:9 | 30–90 s | new products / models | `templates/reference/launch-169` | | **D** Step-by-step tutorial | 16:9 | 3–8 min | "how to…", tool setup | `templates/reference/tutorial-169` | | **E** Multi-host · multi-language · multi-scene | 16:9 | 3–7 min | capability demos, going global | `templates/reference/multihost-169` | Style B has three caption intensities — **restrained / standard / lively**:

Style A learns only the *structure and editing grammar* of popular explainer channels. It never uses a real creator's face, voice, set or lines. --- ## 48 packaging components We measured 25 videos frame by frame (shot detection, opening beats, on-screen text, sound) — full reports in [`references/research/`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/research/).

**Rules distilled from the research** ([`packaging-playbook.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/packaging-playbook.md)): - Cut count can be low, but stimulation can't stop: in the first 30 s, something new every 3–5 s. - First 3 s: the claim or the action — no greeting, no logo. - A BGM bed under everything; sound effects only on events (1–3 per minute in Chinese talking-head channels); 0.6–1.0 s of silence right before a reveal. - For a single-camera digital human, the cheapest pacing is **punch-in cuts** on sentence boundaries (1.0× / 1.18× / 1.32×).

| Group | Components | |---|---| | Opening / hooks | TeaserColdOpen · ColdOpenFreeze · SearchTyping · NumberSpike · SlamText · WordStack · TornStrip · **TextBehind** | | Evidence / data | EvidenceCard · DocFocus · SourceDoc · ZoomFocus · Counter · Odometer · GlassPanel · SpecCard · LineDraw · BarCompare · ReviewCards · ArchiveCards · MapRoute · CompareWipe · PaperCollage | | Annotation / people | HandDraw · CalloutPill · LeaderLabel · TypedNameTag · LowerThird · NamePlate · SourceTag · FreezeFrame | | Rhythm / interaction | PunchInHost · KeywordStack · RetentionCaption · TiltLine · Aside · Danmaku · ReactionPop · MemeWindow · PollPop · GlitchInterstitial · HostFloaters · ProgressChapters · ProgressTracker · ChapterCard · RecapBoard · Countdown · GhostWord | Every component is called by name in a `pack` list, with timings written as `"segment:word"` (e.g. `"3:积分"`), and adapts to 9:16 automatically: ```json "pack": [ { "use": "NumberSpike", "at": "1:不到十块钱", "until": "1:end", "text": "¥9.9/节", "label": "一节课" }, { "use": "Danmaku", "items": [{ "t": "真的假的？", "at": "1:" }, { "t": "AI 还能帮我干活？", "at": "1:教你", "hot": true }] }, { "use": "TextBehind", "src": "main.mp4", "cutout": "main_cut_s4.webm", "cutoutFrom": 17.2, "at": "4:", "until": "4:end", "mode": "count", "lines": [{ "t": "¥99", "font": "en", "color": "#FFE14D", "size": 0.17 }], "count": { "from": 999, "to": 99, "prefix": "¥" } } ] ``` Reference: [`references/packaging.md`](skills/digital-human-koubo/references/packaging.md). Validate before rendering: `python3 scripts/check_edit.py /src`. ### Text behind the presenter

```bash python3 scripts/cutout_video.py public/main.mp4 public/main_cut_s4.webm --from 17.2 --to 22.4 # matte only the seconds you need ``` It works on **medium shots with headroom**. In a selfie close-up the person fills ~89 % of the frame and hides the text — the script warns above 60 %. Mark such segments `"shot": "depth"` and they are generated as medium shots.

--- ## Cost reference (real runs) | Video | Generation | Credits | |---|---|---| | Livestream ad, 9:16, 27 s | 1 scene image + 5 Grok segments (720p) | **482** | | Tutorial Ep2, 16:9, 4:36 | 32 segments (full 720p / PiP 480p) + demos | ~3,250 | | Tutorial Ep3, 16:9, 5:54 | 30 new segments + 7 scene images, 17 segments reused | ~3,409 | Prices at the time of writing: Grok Video 1.5 — 720p 17 credits/s, 480p 10 credits/s; GPT Image 2.5 2k — 23 credits. Always confirm with the agent's live quote. ## Repository structure ``` skills/ digital-human-koubo/ main skill SKILL.md workflow the agent follows persona.json presenters, voice descriptions, prompt templates references/ style menu · packaging · playbook · install · research reports scripts/ build_tasks · rangedl · assemble · align · check_edit · cutout_video voicefx/unify · doctor · new_edit · make_assets templates/ huazi-916/ 9:16 data-driven talking-head template (edit.json) packaging/ 48-component kit + gallery project reference/ launch-169 · tutorial-169 · multihost-169 assets/ style previews · packaging gallery · avatar reference finance-explainer/ Style A engine (episode.json beat sheet, research helpers) docs/ README images, GIF previews, posters ``` ## Known pitfalls (all handled by the skill) - Grok occasionally **burns subtitles** into landscape clips even when told not to → frame check + re-shoot that segment. - whisper writes Chinese numbers as digits (九百九十九 → 999), so accuracy drops but the line is correct → listen before re-shooting. - Renoise's US CDN can truncate parallel downloads → `rangedl.py` downloads in 6 ranges with resume + decode check. - Grok 9:16 720p is **720×1280** — never stretch it to another ratio. - Expo easing never quite reaches the target (99.9 → rounds to 100) → counters snap to the exact value at the end. - Always mute the presenter video track; doubled audio a few ms apart sounds harsh (comb filtering). ## Responsible use - Use only your own face/voice or ones you have **explicit permission** to use. Never impersonate a real person or creator. - Every video carries an "AI digital human" label; scene and animal clips are marked "AI generated". - No made-up numbers, prices, offers or reviews — sample data on screen must be labelled as such. - Don't use web memes, film/TV stills or celebrity images — the meme components use original stickers generated from your own presenter. - Credits are spent only after you approve the quote. ## License & third-party - Code and docs: [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Berryxia (andyhuo520). - **[Remotion](https://www.remotion.dev/)** is used for rendering and has its own license: free for individuals and companies of up to 3 people; larger companies need a [company license](https://www.remotion.pro/). - Animated emoji: [Google Noto Emoji Animation](https://googlefonts.github.io/noto-emoji-animation/) (CC BY 4.0) — credit "Animated emoji: Google Noto" in your videos. - Maps: [world-atlas](https://github.com/topojson/world-atlas) (ISC; data from Natural Earth, public domain) · [d3-geo](https://github.com/d3/d3-geo), [topojson-client](https://github.com/topojson/topojson-client) (ISC). For maps involving China's borders in formally published content, check against applicable local standards. - Speech recognition: [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp) (MIT). Generation runs on [Renoise](https://renoise.ai/mcp?utm_medium=xcom&utm_source=official) (your account, your credits); optional TTS by [Xiaomi MiMo](https://platform.xiaomimimo.com/). - Course screenshots in the WorkBuddy demo come from the author's own course. Demo videos are the author's own work; please don't re-upload them as your own. See [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md) for details. ---

# WildRig Multi
multi algo miner for AMD, NVIDIA and Intel gpu's

[Discord community](https://discord.gg/ZGDaQ6edXb)

# KNOWN ISSUES
- **nexapow** is not supported on AMD gpu's with pre-RDNA architecture
- **evohash** and some other x-like algorithms produce incorrect shares on NVIDIA Blackwell gpu's
- any report is welcome! :)

# SUPPORTED GPU's
## AMD:
- **GCN 2nd gen**: Radeon R7 260, R9 290, R9 295X2, R7 360, R9 390
- **GCN 3rd gen**: Radeon R9 285, R9 380, R9 Fury, R9 Nano
- **GCN 4th gen**: Radeon RX 460, 470, 480, 550, 560, 570, 580, 590
- **GCN 5th gen**: Radeon Vega 56, Vega 64, Vega FE, Radeon VII
- **RDNA 1st gen**: Radeon RX 5500, 5600, 5700
- **RDNA 2nd gen**: Radeon RX 6500, 6600, 6700, 6750, 6800, 6900, 6950
- **RDNA 3rd gen**: Radeon RX 7600, 7700, 7800, 7900
- **RDNA 4th gen**: Radeon RX 9070

Pitcairn, Tahiti and other old cards of **GCN 1st gen**(like HD 78x0, HD 79x0, R7 265, R9 270, R9 280, R9 370, etc.) are not supported and won't be, because they are too old and need additional work.

## NVIDIA:
- **Maxwell**: GTX 750, GTX 9x0 series, Titan X, Tesla M-series
- **Pascal**: GTX 10x0 series, Titan Xp, Tesla P-series, P106-090, P106-100, P104-100, P104-101, P102-100, P102-101
- **Volta**: Tesla V-series, CMP 100HX-210
- **Turing**: GTX 16x0 series, RTX 20x0 series, Tesla T-series, Quadro Turing, CMP 30HX, CMP 40HX, CMP 50HX
- **Ampere**: RTX 30x0 series, Quadro Ampere, CMP 70HX, CMP 90HX, CMP 170HX
- **Ada Lovelace**: RTX 40x0 series, Quadro Ada
- **Blackwell**: RTX 50x0 series

Minimum driver versio is 452.39+ on Windows and 450.80.02+ on Linux. Supported list of gpu's is much longer, but not all of them have default intensity value, so use parameter *--gpu-instensity* to get better hashrate

## INTEL:
- **Intel Arc Alchemist**: A310(E), A350(M,E), A370(M,E), A380(E), A530M, A550M, A570M, A580(E), A730M, A750(E), A770(M)
- **Intel Arc Alchemist Pro**: A30M, A40/A50, A60M, A60
- **Intel Arc Battlemage**: B570, B580
- **Intel Data Center GPU**: Flex 140, Flex 170

# SUPPORTED ALGORITHMS
- anime
- bitcore, blake2s, bmw512
- c11, curvehash
- evrprogpow
- firopow
- ghostrider
- heavyhash, hex, hmq1725
- kawpow
- lyra2v2
- megabtx, memehash, meowpow
- nexapow, nist5
- pearlhash, phi, progpowz, progpow-sero, progpow-telestai
- qhash, quark, qubit
- sha256, sha256csm, sha256d, sha256q, sha256t, sha512256d, shandwich256, skein2, skunkhash, skydoge
- timetravel, tribus
- x11, x11k, x12, x13, x14, x15, x16r, x16rv2, x16rt, x16s, x17, x18, x20r, x21s, x22i, x25x, x33

# DEV-FEE:

All algorithms are zero fee except listed below.

- **0.75%**:
  - evrprogpow
  - firopow
  - kawpow
  - meowpow
  - nexapow
  - progpow-quai
  - progpow-sero
  - progpow-telestai
  - progpowz
- **1.00%**:
  - curvehash
  - ghostrider
  - mike
- **2.00%**:
  - skydoge
  - qhash

# OPTIONS
```
Usage: wildrig [OPTIONS]

  Some parameters can be set per gpu, use comma to separate each gpu and * to skip

Options:
  -a, --algo ALGO               specify the hash algorithm to use
      --benchmark                run offline benchmark
      --benchmark-hashorder      run offline benchmark and/or set hash order for benchmark
      --benchmark-epoch          run offline benchmark and/or set epoch for benchmark
      --benchmark-block          run offline benchmark and/or set block for benchmark
      --benchmark-timeout        run offline benchmark and/or set how long to run benchmark in seconds(default: 0)

  -o, --url URL                  URL of mining server
      --proxy                    set ip:port to connect via SOCKS5 proxy
  -O, --userpass U:P             username:password pair for mining server
  -u, --user USERNAME            username for mining server
  -p, --pass PASSWORD            password for mining server
  -w, --worker WORKERNAME        worker name(progpow variants only)
  -r, --retries N                number of times to retry before switch to backup server (default: 1)
  -R, --retry-pause N            time to pause between retries (default: 5)
```

items.description: Self-hosted web and AI crawler analytics for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). Track visitors, AI search referrals, crawl logs, content coverage, and conversions. Jointly published by 猎看科技 · 北京日报社智源GEO. MIT licensed.
items.readme:
# GEOInflow

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Self-hosted web and AI crawler analytics for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).

**Jointly published by 猎看科技 · 北京日报社智源GEO**

[Quick start](docs/getting-started.en.md) · [Deployment](docs/deployment.en.md) · [AI crawler analytics](docs/ai-crawler-analytics.md) · [Architecture](docs/system-overview.md) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

GEOInflow brings website visitors, AI search referrals, server crawl logs, and content inventories into a shared website context. It helps teams understand which AI crawlers visit their sites, which pages they request, which important pages have no observed crawl activity, where requests fail, and how AI search contributes visitors and conversions.

The system includes browser tracking, account permissions, GEO reports, crawler evidence, log collection, and analytics acceleration. The current product version is **v1.2**, with build version **1.2.0**. Application source code is distributed under the [MIT license](LICENSE).

Quick start and deployment guides are available in English and Simplified Chinese. Other linked reference guides are currently in Simplified Chinese.

## Introduction video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81e57cc4-3441-4e5f-b2fb-cd929c6c27bd

## What you can use it for

| Question | Available data | Actions it can inform |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which AI platforms visit the site? | Crawler identity, purpose, provider, request volume, verification status, and trends | Distinguish training, search, and user-triggered requests to understand how content is accessed |
| Which pages are crawled repeatedly? | Page rankings, repeat requests, directory distribution, and recent activity | Review frequently requested paths, invalid URLs, and content structure |
| Have important pages been crawled? | Import sitemap / CSV / JSON inventories and compare them with observed logs | Check entry points, internal links, robots rules, and responses |
| Are crawler requests succeeding? | HTTP status, GET / HEAD, caching, latency, errors, and risk signals | Investigate blocked requests, origin errors, coverage drops, and source interruptions |
| What does AI search bring to the site? | AI referral sessions, landing pages, goals, and conversions | Observe changes in real traffic and business outcomes |
| Is there enough evidence for a conclusion? | Identity evidence, source coverage, gaps, missing inputs, and estimates | Review results over the same data scope and keep evidence gaps explicit |

GEOInflow is designed for company websites, content sites, media publishers, developer documentation, and GEO teams managing multiple sites. Operators can work at the website and page level, while maintainers can inspect ingestion, queues, source quality, and calculation methods.

## AI crawler analytics

### Crawler identity and purpose

The built-in catalog covers OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, Google, Microsoft, ByteDance, Baidu, Kimi, Tencent Hunyuan, and other providers. It also retains observations of traditional search crawlers and other bots.

The catalog records platforms, products, and request identities separately. Training, AI search, and user-triggered access describe request purposes; AI workbenches and personal agents describe product types. These dimensions can overlap. Active entries depend on the administrator-published catalog and each website's configuration.

Declared User-Agent strings, matches against official IP ranges, and available DNS or trusted edge evidence are stored independently. A User-Agent claim alone is insufficient to confirm a source. Historical records without verification evidence retain an unknown status.

### Crawl activity and content coverage

Review requested-page rankings, observed pages, repeated requests, directory distribution, leading crawlers, recent activity, and content freshness. Import a content inventory to measure observed crawl coverage and AI blind spots against a known set of pages.

Identity, purpose, and product-type filters apply before aggregation and pagination. Cards, tables, comparisons, and exports use the same conditions. Path observations and inferred results retain their estimate labels.

### Investigate access problems with evidence

HTTP responses, caching, latency, response bytes, collection continuity, and risk findings are shown separately. Teams can record handling status, notes, deferrals, and resumptions, then review the relevant time windows and evidence.

Access policies support robots / Nginx configuration exports. Supported Cloudflare controls require separate Zone credentials, a preview, explicit confirmation, background execution, and a read-back of the remote state. Provider plans, permissions, and available fields must be checked in the deployed environment.

### AI referrals and business outcomes

Browser tracking recognizes supported AI search referrals and combines them with landing pages, events, goals, and conversions. Crawler requests, referral sessions, and conversions are measured separately. Cross-source associations retain their comparability limits.

**Crawl logs establish observed access. Indexing, model training, answer citations, recommendation rankings, and customer acquisition each require their own evidence.**

See the [AI crawler analytics guide](docs/ai-crawler-analytics.md) for metrics, workflows, and limitations.

## Website analytics

| Capability | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Pageviews and visitors | PV, UV, visits, referrals, geography, devices, browsers, and content performance |
| Events and conversions | Custom events, goals, funnels, visitor paths, attribution, and revenue analysis |
| Extended analysis | Search engines, referral keywords, UTM, performance, heatmaps, retention, and audiences |
| Collaboration | Websites, personal and team spaces, permissions, workspaces, dashboards, and public sharing |
| Exports | CSV / JSON / ZIP for the selected scope, preserving fields, states, and sensitive-data handling |
| AI assistance | Optional model connections and conversations based on website facts, disabled by default |
| Operations and governance | Ingestion checks, historical data repair, analytics acceleration, and source and rule versioning |

The application supports Simplified Chinese and English. The main date ranges are Today / 7 days / 30 days, and the default analytics timezone is `Asia/Shanghai`. The first full sign-in confirms the country and city timezone; later requests use the account's saved timezone to define today. Realtime visitors cover the most recent 30 minutes, and retention uses calendar months.

Browser metrics share a common traffic-quality policy. Empty data, missing integrations, unknown values, estimates, and unsupported capabilities are shown as distinct states. Demo websites are explicitly labeled. See [page coverage](docs/ui-coverage.md) for the feature matrix and [date ranges and timezones](docs/date-ranges.md) for date definitions.

## How data enters the system

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Website browser script] --> C[Application and ingestion APIs]
  B[Server / CDN logs] --> C
  D[sitemap / CSV / JSON inventory] --> C
  C --> E[(PostgreSQL)]
  E --> F[Log and analytics workers]
  F --> E
  E --> G[Reports and published results]
  H[(Redis cache)] --- G
  G --> I[GEO / visitor / content analytics]
  G --> J[Permission-controlled sharing and exports]
```

The browser script collects pageviews, events, and enabled extended data. Server and CDN logs add crawler requests that do not run browser scripts. Content inventories provide a known set of pages. Each input can be connected independently, and the corresponding analysis states its limitations when a source is missing.

Log processing retains sources, classifications, and verification evidence. Analytics workers use pre-aggregation, exact visit facts, and durable results to reduce repeated calculations. Standard dashboards and heavier analysis have separate admission controls. Frequently used ranges are prewarmed, and published results remain available during background updates. See the [architecture guide](docs/system-overview.md).

## Quick deployment

Start Docker Engine / Docker Desktop and Docker Compose V2, and ensure that image and dependency download sources are reachable. After obtaining the source code, run this command from the project root:

```sh
sh scripts/liekan-deploy.sh
```

The script generates a private `.env` and random secrets, builds the application image, runs migrations, and starts the application, log worker, analytics worker, PostgreSQL, and Redis. The default address is:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:3002
```

For a fresh installation, the initial username is `admin` and the initial password is `liekan`. Change the password after signing in, then create a website using the ingestion guide. Upgrades preserve existing customized passwords and accounts.

To try the bundled example after the application starts, run:

```sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.liekan.yml exec app node scripts/liekan-seed-demo.mjs
```

The example is named “猎看官网（示例数据）”. It initializes from the processed dataset included with the source. On first import, its timestamps are shifted to make the data convenient to explore. Repeated runs preserve existing data and deletion state. See the [default demo guide](docs/default-demo.md).

Production access requires a domain, HTTPS, and a trusted reverse proxy. Browser PV collection can continue without a trusted IP ingress, while identity metrics such as UV require reliable ingress evidence. Automatic log ingestion and optional AI analysis have separate configuration requirements.

The [deployment guide](docs/deployment.en.md) covers services, configuration, proxies, backups, and upgrades. The [quick start](docs/getting-started.en.md) explains how to connect the first website.

## Keeping analytics current

The main Today dashboards read published results every 30 seconds and show the actual data cutoff. Reads pause while the page is hidden or offline. Realtime visitors use their own refresh interval, while heavier analyses such as heatmaps and retention use longer background windows.

Completed results use browser, process, Redis, and PostgreSQL persistence. Common date ranges and pages share query conditions. Capacity safeguards govern eviction of older windows, idle failed tasks pause automatic retries, and initial calculations can finish through durable background tasks. Updates retain statistics permissions and checks for source quality, dates, and rule versions.

Initial calculations, cache hits, and background updates have different costs. Actual performance depends on data volume, coverage construction, the database, and cache state. After deployment, the Analytics Acceleration page shows tasks and coverage. See [analytics acceleration](docs/analytics-acceleration.md) and [caching](docs/analytics-cache.md).

## Self-hosting and scope

- Core website analytics and crawler identification can run on your own infrastructure without a model API key.
- Browser tracking is cookieless by default. Optional recording, event properties, and business integrations use the data scope configured for each deployment.
- AI analysis is disabled by default. When enabled, users choose model connections and website materials. See the [AI configuration guide](docs/ai.md) for the data sent to models.
- GEO Weight is in Beta. It uses qualified AI content access from the most recent 30 complete calendar days, with a documented formula, evidence, and limitations. The [weight guide](docs/geo-weight.md) defines the fixed policy and applicable scope.
- GEO extensions, supplemental journeys, complete exports, and analytics acceleration primarily target PostgreSQL. Retained ClickHouse, link, and pixel endpoints follow their existing protocols; support for each GEO extension must be checked separately.
- Automatic server collection requires public HTTPS, an ingestion secret, and signed installation assets. Cloudflare integration also requires OAuth, permissions, and the relevant provider capabilities.
- Search impressions, actual rankings, model-answer citations, training inclusion, and article completion rates require additional data. The detailed guides define the observations and scores this project provides.

## Development and maintenance

Development uses Node.js **22.23.4**, pnpm **12.3.4**, and PostgreSQL. Prepare an independent database and private configuration using the [deployment guide](docs/deployment.en.md), then run the following commands. This example uses the separate development port `3302`:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build:db
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm liekan:migrate
pnpm liekan:queue-bootstrap
pnpm build:openapi
pnpm build:packages
pnpm build:tracker
pnpm build:recorder
pnpm liekan:build-worker
pnpm dev --port 3302
```

Start the log and analytics workers in separate terminals as described in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Development workers and the web application use the same private environment configuration.

Product pages live in `src/components/liekan`, data contracts in `src/lib/liekan/contracts`, and upstream query and permission adapters in `src/lib/liekan/upstream`. New structures use incremental project migrations. Applied migrations remain immutable. The `liekan` technical identifiers, collection protocols, and existing workspace package names retain compatibility.

For issue reports, contributions, scoped verification, and upstream synchronization, see [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), the [documentation index](docs/README.md), and [upstream maintenance](docs/upstream-upgrade.md).

## License and notices

GEOInflow application source code and project documentation use the [MIT license](LICENSE), permitting use, modification, and redistribution, including commercial use, subject to its notice requirements. The full license text governs these permissions.

GEOInflow is jointly published by 猎看科技 and 北京日报社智源GEO. Original copyright and license text are retained with the source. See the [upstream notes](docs/upstream.md) for the project's origin and compatibility relationship.

Dependencies, fonts, and geographic datasets retain their own licenses. See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). The default geographic dataset is DB-IP City Lite, with its attribution and CC BY 4.0 license retained. Supplied MaxMind or other geographic databases must comply with their respective data terms. Runtime configuration, real visitor data, database backups, private keys, and privately supplied geographic databases are outside the source release.

# Nyxis

English | [日本語](README.ja.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-v0.1.0-orange.svg)](https://github.com/NyxFoundation/nyxis)
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-under%20development-yellow.svg)](ASSUMPTIONS.md)
[![Lean](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lean-v4.34.1-0052cc.svg?logo=lean&logoColor=white)](lean-toolchain)
[![Cedar](https://img.shields.io/badge/policies-Cedar-6f42c1.svg)](https://www.cedarpolicy.com/)
[![Formally verified](https://img.shields.io/badge/authorization-formally%20verified-brightgreen.svg)](ASSUMPTIONS.md)
[![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-Supabase-4169E1.svg?logo=postgresql&logoColor=white)](https://supabase.com/)
[![Supabase Auth](https://img.shields.io/badge/auth-Supabase%20Auth-3ECF8E.svg?logo=supabase&logoColor=white)](https://supabase.com/auth)
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/NyxFoundation/nyxis?style=social)](https://github.com/NyxFoundation/nyxis)

**A Lean backend framework whose authorization safety is formally proven.**

Nyxis lets solo developers who ship web applications written by AI agents release them with confidence about authorization. The only things a developer writes and approves are a [Cedar](https://www.cedarpolicy.com/) schema and policies. Handlers can be written as usual by Claude Code or similar tools, and the developer never has to write Lean.

Every backend built on Nyxis comes with a formal proof of the following:

> No sequence of HTTP requests can cause an authenticated principal to read, modify, delete, or grant access to data beyond its legitimate permissions.

The Lean kernel checks this property on every `lake build`. Reviewing and auditing authorization comes down to reading the schema and policies and confirming that the proof checks.

> [!NOTE]
> Nyxis is under active development (v0.1.1). The scope of the guarantee and the assumptions trusted outside the proof are spelled out in [ASSUMPTIONS.md](ASSUMPTIONS.md). Read it before using Nyxis in production.

## How it works

1. **Write and approve a Cedar schema and policies.** The schema doubles as the table definition (entity type = table, attribute = column), and each action carries exactly one effect defined by Nyxis.
2. **Write handlers (or let an AI agent write them).** Handlers have the Nyxis type `Nyxis.Handler`, and their only effect is calling actions on the authorization layer. They cannot perform IO or reach the database directly.
3. **Run `lake build`.** Building also binds the app to the approved sources, audits the application code, and checks the proofs.
4. **Call it from any client.** Clients call the backend over HTTP with a Supabase Auth JWT. The frontend lives outside Nyxis as an ordinary HTTP client.

An example schema (from the official bulletin-board sample):

```cedar
entity User = { "admin": Bool };
entity Post = { "author": User, "title": String, "body": String, "published": Bool };

@effect("update Post(title, body)")
action "editPost" appliesTo { principal: [User], resource: [Post] };
```

An example policy:

```cedar
// Only the author or an admin can edit, publish, or delete a post.
@id("manage-post")
permit (
  principal is User,
  action in [Action::"editPost", Action::"publishPost", Action::"deletePost"],
  resource is Post
) when { resource.author == principal || principal.admin };
```

Besides `read`, `list`, `insert`, `update` (with an explicit column list), and `delete`, effects include file storage via signed URLs, email notifications, and external API calls. All of them go through the authorization layer and are covered by the same theorem. Nyxis determines the principal from the JWT, the resource from the current database row, and the current time and unique IDs per request, so handlers cannot forge any of them.

## Requirements

- Lean 4 via [elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan) (the version is pinned in `lean-toolchain`)
- Python 3.12 or later, the OpenSSL CLI, and a C compiler
- pkg-config and the development files for libpq and libcrypto (on macOS, `brew install libpq`; because Homebrew's libpq is keg-only, add `$(brew --prefix libpq)/lib/pkgconfig` to `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`)
- At runtime: PostgreSQL (Supabase) and Supabase Auth

## Build

```sh
python3 scripts/prepare-dependencies.py   # fetch pinned dependencies into .lake/vendor/, verified by SHA256
lake build                                # build and check the core, proofs, and tests
```

See [docs/dependencies.md](docs/dependencies.md) for dependency preparation and [docs/local-supabase.md](docs/local-supabase.md) for setting up a local Supabase (both in Japanese).

## Using Nyxis in your application

Nyxis is a standalone package you pull in with Lake's `require`. Your application package contains only the schema, policies, handlers, and startup code, and none of Nyxis's code. Nyxis resolves its pinned dependencies from `.lake/vendor/` inside its own checkout, so first run the build steps above in a clone of this repository, then require it by path (as the official samples do):

```lean
require nyxis from "<path to your Nyxis clone>"
```

Link arguments for libpq do not propagate to the requiring package, so copy the `postgresLinkArgs` definition from the root `lakefile.lean` into your application's `lakefile.lean`. Declare the approved sources with `nyxis_approved`, and put `nyxis_check_app` at the end of a final module that imports every application module. See the official samples for the concrete layout.

## Official samples

- [`examples/bulletin-board/`](examples/bulletin-board/README.md): a bulletin board with published and draft posts, Google OAuth login, and granting and revoking admin rights. It ships with a Next.js frontend, so you can watch the policies allow and deny requests as you use the UI.
- [`examples/team-docs/`](examples/team-docs/README.md): document sharing within organizations, with memberships and roles, timestamps, filtered and paginated lists, attachments, email notifications, and external API calls. Backend only for now.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Nyxis/` | The core (Cedar parsing, authorization layer, runtime, connection code) and proofs. The main theorem is `Nyxis.Runtime.authorization_safety` |
| `Test/` | Core tests. `Test/Axioms.lean` checks the axioms of every theorem |
| `scripts/` | Dependency preparation and integration check scripts |
| `examples/` | Official samples |
| `docs/` | Proof catalog, responsibilities of the connection code, design notes |
| `supabase/` | Local Supabase configuration |

## Documentation

Apart from the README and ASSUMPTIONS, documentation is currently written in Japanese.

- [ASSUMPTIONS.md](ASSUMPTIONS.md): scope of the guarantee and the assumptions trusted outside the proof
- [docs/proofs.md](docs/proofs.md): catalog of proven theorems and what each one does not state
- [docs/connection.md](docs/connection.md): how the connection code upholds the assumptions

## License

[MIT License](LICENSE) © 2026 Nyx Foundation

# Awesome SuperMimic [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2610.28480-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480) [![License: CC0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC0_1.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](CONTRIBUTING.md) **A curated collection of SuperMimic implementations, extensions, demos, and resources.** English · [简体中文](README_zh-CN.md) [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480) · [Official website](https://supermimic.github.io/) · [Interactive demo](https://supermimic.github.io/demo/) · [Community projects](#community-projects)


World-model predictions


Simulation
Real G1

Original footage: SuperMimic authors · Click a preview for the full video · Media credits

Start with the original work below, then choose an implementation by framework and task. This is a community-maintained resource list; the linked implementations are credited to their own authors. ## Contents - [Original SuperMimic](#original-supermimic) - [Community projects](#community-projects) - [Related methods and baselines](#related-methods-and-baselines) - [Data and learning resources](#data-and-learning-resources) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Citation](#citation) - [Acknowledgements and license](#acknowledgements-and-license) ## Original SuperMimic **[SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480)**
Qiayuan Liao, Yiyang Shao, Junfeng Long, Kevin Zakka, Roberto Horowitz, Pieter Abbeel, and Koushil Sreenath.
**UC Berkeley · CoRL 2026 Oral** [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480) · [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.28480) · [Project](https://supermimic.github.io/) · [Video](https://supermimic.github.io/media/real/film-1080.mp4) · [Browser demo](https://supermimic.github.io/demo/) SuperMimic learns shared humanoid dynamics from simulator transitions and improves a motion-tracking policy through short imagined rollouts. The world model and policy are updated in the same training loop; policy gradients pass through the learned model. [Method overview](https://supermimic.github.io/#loop).

Original paper, Figure 2 · Framework, p. 4 · Algorithm A.1, p. 15

The world model is fit on **8-step replay windows**; the policy and critic learn from **32-step imagined rollouts**. During the policy update, model weights stay fixed while gradients pass through the model to the policy. Blue dashed arrows show gradients; ❄️ marks frozen weights and 🔥 marks weights being trained in that phase. The authors report surpassing SONIC's released-checkpoint return after **3 hours on one H100**, with **25 / 129,514 failed motions**, and **0 / 129,514** after 9.8 hours on two H100s. These are training-motion coverage results, with different training hardware and data from SONIC. See the [official results and compute accounting](https://supermimic.github.io/#compute). **Official code status — checked 2026-10-26:** the official website links the paper, video, and browser demo, but does not link a training-code repository. The projects below are community implementations and extensions. ## Community projects **29 community projects**, grouped by purpose. Descriptions were checked against upstream documentation and selected source files on **2026-10-26**; each entry links to the reviewed source revision. Results and demos are upstream reports; this list has not independently rerun the experiments. - 🔬 **[Independent reproductions](#independent-reproductions)** — **3 projects** · Reproduce and evaluate the original method. - 🧩 **[Methods and task extensions](#methods-and-task-extensions)** — **11 projects** · Explore new methods, tasks and control settings. - 🛠️ **[Frameworks, robot ports and deployment](#frameworks-robot-ports-and-deployment)** — **12 projects** · Find a stack, robot port or deployment path. - 💡 **[Inspired experiments](#inspired-experiments)** — **3 projects** · Transfer ideas to other control problems. ## Independent reproductions Reimplementations of the original method, with training, evaluation and reproduction notes. ### supermimic_vibed [Repository](https://github.com/zita-ch/supermimic_vibed) · [Setup and usage](https://github.com/zita-ch/supermimic_vibed/blob/a1508d42c9d1699a52e8233ab16d08c488441ab9/README.md#setup) · [Results](https://github.com/zita-ch/supermimic_vibed/blob/a1508d42c9d1699a52e8233ab16d08c488441ab9/README.md#result-lafan1-40-clips-one-rtx-pro-6000-blackwell) - **By Chong Zhang.** An independent G1 implementation on Isaac Lab 3, with a kit-less setup, training, full-clip evaluation and rendering tools. - **Upstream report:** On 40 LAFAN1 clips, normalized return **0.829** and **0 / 40 failures** after **1.47 hours on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell**. - **Useful context:** The author describes it as a rapid, unreviewed reproduction. Documented deviations include disabled self-collisions, bf16 MLP computation and an extra reference-root orientation input. [Source snapshot](https://github.com/zita-ch/supermimic_vibed/blob/a1508d42c9d1699a52e8233ab16d08c488441ab9/README.md).
Simulation · LAFAN1 highlights
### SuperMimic-Reproduced [Repository](https://github.com/CuboiLeo/SuperMimic-Reproduced) · [Setup](https://github.com/CuboiLeo/SuperMimic-Reproduced/blob/d9be385b3eeb13a638fb33fb200d3bfd9be9839f/README.md#环境) · [Experiment log](https://github.com/CuboiLeo/SuperMimic-Reproduced/blob/d9be385b3eeb13a638fb33fb200d3bfd9be9839f/docs/EXPERIMENTS.md) - **By CuboiLeo.** A from-scratch mjlab implementation for G1, with Chinese reproduction notes, LAFAN1/BONES-SEED processing, multi-GPU training and an interactive replay viewer. - **Upstream report:** With anchor-relative observations, one RTX 5090 reaches LAFAN1 return **0.824**, **5 / 40 failures** at **1.66 hours**, and **0.904**, **3 / 40 failures** at **3.3 hours**. - **Useful context:** The paper-observation run reports **0.56** and **9 / 40 failures** at 1.8 hours. These observation settings are not equivalent; the reported BONES-SEED scores use a 2,000-motion evaluation subset. [Source snapshot](https://github.com/CuboiLeo/SuperMimic-Reproduced/blob/d9be385b3eeb13a638fb33fb200d3bfd9be9839f/README.md).
Report screenshot · paper-style and anchor-relative observations
### supermimic_vibe [Repository](https://github.com/dhmbb2/supermimic_vibe) · [Setup](https://github.com/dhmbb2/supermimic_vibe/blob/072f0910dadc9d95c720e625b546120e9ce917c9/README.md#setup) · [Results log](https://github.com/dhmbb2/supermimic_vibe/blob/072f0910dadc9d95c720e625b546120e9ce917c9/notes/RESULTS.md) - **By dhmbb2.** An independent G1 reproduction in mjlab, covering PPO-Sim/PPO-WM comparisons, horizon and critic ablations, push recovery and velocity-control experiments. - **Upstream report:** On one RTX A6000, LAFAN1 normalized return reaches **0.833 at 1.34 hours** and **0.946 with 0 / 40 failures at 12 hours**, using complete deterministic clip evaluation. - **Useful context:** The experiment log distinguishes reproduced, partial and pending results. BONES-SEED remains data-gated, hardware transfer is out of scope, and the A6000 timings are not H100 timings. [Source snapshot](https://github.com/dhmbb2/supermimic_vibe/blob/072f0910dadc9d95c720e625b546120e9ce917c9/README.md).
Report screenshot · reproduction and ablations on one RTX A6000
## Methods and task extensions Changes to the method, new tasks and focused experiments in perception, morphology and interaction. ### MorphMimic [Repository](https://github.com/lzyang2000/morphmimic) · [Setup](https://github.com/lzyang2000/morphmimic/blob/2e35049e9519e511889ef987e4acde55d4f5b017/README.md#setup) · [Method differences](https://github.com/lzyang2000/morphmimic/blob/2e35049e9519e511889ef987e4acde55d4f5b017/README.md#differences-from-supermimic) - **By Lizhi Yang et al.** Extends SuperMimic in mjlab to share a world model, a policy, or both across G1, X2 Ultra and T2, conditioning the networks on robot morphology. - **What it provides:** Supports full-motion tracking and sparse five-point goals for the pelvis, wrists and ankles; the project includes a browser demo and teleoperation/deployment instructions. - **Useful context:** Robots are mapped to a common 29-joint layout. The README documents changes to termination modeling, normalization, warm-up and actuator-delay randomization. [Source snapshot](https://github.com/lzyang2000/morphmimic/blob/2e35049e9519e511889ef987e4acde55d4f5b017/README.md).
Simulation · one shared policy for G1 / X2 Ultra / T2 [Video](https://lzyang2000.github.io/morphmimic/static/videos/morphmimic.mp4) · [Interactive demo](https://lzyang2000.github.io/morphmimic/demo/)
### allmimic [Repository](https://github.com/Shimingyi/allmimic) · [Install](https://github.com/Shimingyi/allmimic/blob/cb334ff674b2f57248f33f8c21b7fb526fbdf8cc/README.md#install) · [Results](https://github.com/Shimingyi/allmimic/blob/cb334ff674b2f57248f33f8c21b7fb526fbdf8cc/README.md#results) - **By Shimingyi.** Builds on supermimic_vibe for G1 in mjlab, mixing residual upper-body actions with absolute leg actions, weighting world-model losses and balancing motion sampling. - **Upstream report:** With the recommended preset on one RTX 4090, full-length LAFAN1 evaluation reports **0 / 40 failures and return 0.91 after 0.83 hours**; training time excludes evaluation. - **Useful context:** The recommended preset changes the method and data sampling. The 306-hard-motion-only run and full BONES-SEED training are separate experiments. [Source snapshot](https://github.com/Shimingyi/allmimic/blob/cb334ff674b2f57248f33f8c21b7fb526fbdf8cc/README.md).
Simulation · challenging motion clips
### SuperMimic on LocoMuJoCo [Repository](https://github.com/Alchedata/supermimic-locomujoco) · [Setup](https://github.com/Alchedata/supermimic-locomujoco/blob/cc1375d48a38bde062d088ffd132122e0cd7b7da/README.md#setup) · [Results](https://github.com/Alchedata/supermimic-locomujoco/blob/cc1375d48a38bde062d088ffd132122e0cd7b7da/README.md#results-at-5k) - **By Alchedata.** Ports the method to H1 with JAX and LocoMuJoCo, comparing an MLP baseline with residual-expert, action-sensitivity and trust-aware world models. - **Upstream report:** Publishes fixed 5,000-iteration checkpoints evaluated over 160 episodes, including both successful seeds and a residual-expert run that became stuck with saturated actions. - **Useful context:** The reward is LocoMuJoCo episode return, not the G1 normalized tracking score. Recovery interventions and their continuation controls are recorded separately. [Source snapshot](https://github.com/Alchedata/supermimic-locomujoco/blob/cc1375d48a38bde062d088ffd132122e0cd7b7da/README.md).
Report screenshot · fixed 5k checkpoints, 160 evaluation episodes
### Rethinking SuperMimic [Repository](https://github.com/btx0424/rethinking-supermimic) · [Installation](https://github.com/btx0424/rethinking-supermimic/blob/ecdaeb6a916a16cf7eb69b19226c17be31a6bc27/README.md#installation) · [Implementation comparison](https://github.com/btx0424/rethinking-supermimic/blob/ecdaeb6a916a16cf7eb69b19226c17be31a6bc27/README.md#ours-the-paper-and-supermimic_vibed) - **By btx0424.** Studies goal conditioning for G1 in mjlab: concatenating the goal with proprioception versus using FiLM to modulate the policy layers. - **Useful context:** Provides configurable observations, anchor choices and Viser playback. # OmarchyTV

**An Omarchy-style home screen for Android TV, featuring a native Omarchy TUI Grok Bot assistant, 26 MIT themes with 4K wallpapers, a desktop link to your Omarchy PC / Mac, a native MCP server, and an Android smartphone wireless installer.**

Created by **[Marco Porro](https://www.marcoporro.it)** ([x.com/MarcoPorro](https://x.com/MarcoPorro) · [www.marcoporro.it](https://www.marcoporro.it))

Official Synchronized Repositories: **[GitHub (`github.com/piermark/omarchytv`)](https://github.com/piermark/omarchytv)** · **[GitLab (`gitlab.com/piermark/omarchytv`)](https://gitlab.com/piermark/omarchytv)**

Published: **25 October 2026 (beta)** · Version **2.12.0-beta** (`versionCode 20` — Android TV, PC/Mac Plugin & Mobile Companion) / **2.11.0-testing** (LG webOS experimental) · License **MIT**

> [!WARNING]
> **BETA SOFTWARE: THINGS MAY NOT WORK.** OmarchyTV has been tested on several devices (Sony KD-55XE9005 on Android 9,
> Google TV Streamer on Android 14, Sharp AQUOS, Noblex/Hisense on Android 11) plus the Android TV emulator. Expect rough edges, missing features on some TVs and bugs. It never roots or uninstalls
> anything, and you can always switch back to the stock home screen (see [INSTALL](launcher/docs/INSTALL.md)), but use it at your own risk.

---

## What's New in `2.12.0-beta` (`versionCode 20`)

1. **Native Grok Bot · Omarchy TUI (`AskActivity`) on the TV Home Shelf:**
   - Clicking the **Grok Bot** tile (`grokbot@tv:~$ > GROK BOT [ omarchy · tui ]`) on the TV Home shelf — or selecting `Grok Bot (Omarchy TUI)` in the menu — opens a **native Omarchy-styled TUI assistant window** (`BoxView` 2 px border, `btop`-style legend `grok bot · omarchy tui [<theme>]`, translucent theme surface over the live 4K `WallpaperView`, `CaskaydiaMono` font, and `grokbot@omarchytv:~$` prompt) instead of jumping straight into a raw web browser.
   - **Standalone Local TV & MCP Control (works offline without a PC):** Switch any of the 26 MIT themes (`theme jade-horse`, `theme year-of-the-horse`, `theme hermarchy`, `next theme`, `themes`), cycle 4K wallpapers (`wallpaper`), launch or configure the 37 `tte.js` ASCII screensavers (`screensaver`, `speed slow|normal|fast`), launch installed TV apps or Live TV (`open YouTube`, `open TV`, `apps`), or inspect TV/network/MCP status (`status`, `mcp`) via voice, keyboard, or 1-click D-pad quick chips (`[ ⏭ next theme ]`, `[ 🖼 wallpaper ]`, `[ ✦ screensaver ]`, `[ 📊 status ]`, `[ 📦 apps ]`, `[ ❓ help ]`).
   - **Paired PC / Mac AI Bridge (`OmarchyLink`):** Automatically forwards open-ended AI questions over the encrypted LAN link to your already-authenticated PC/Mac CLI (`grok`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `hermes`, or local `ollama`) and streams the reply typewriter-style in the TUI terminal.
   - **Optional 1-Click Full Browser WebApp Mode (`[ 🌐 grok.com ]` / `[ 🌐 web ▾ ]`):** Whenever you want the full web interface, select `[ 🌐 grok.com ]` or `[ 🌐 web ▾ ]` inside the TUI header (or from `> Grok Bot & AI`) to open **Grok Web** (`grok.com`), **Grok (X)** (`x.com/i/grok`), **ChatGPT** (`chatgpt.com`), **Claude** (`claude.ai`), or **Hermes** (`hermes.nousresearch.com`) in the sandboxed `:web` process (`WebAppActivity`) with persistent cookies/DOM storage and D-pad cursor.
2. **26 100%-MIT Themes & Bundled 4K Wallpapers + `Sync PC wallpaper` Toggle:**
   - Added 3 new 100%-MIT community themes with all their original 4K wallpapers: DHH's **[`jade-horse`](https://github.com/dhh/omarchy-jade-horse-theme)** and **[`year-of-the-horse`](https://github.com/dhh/omarchy-year-of-the-horse-theme)**, plus Archer Clawbot's **[`hermarchy`](https://github.com/archer-clawbot/omarchy-hermarchy-theme)**.
   - Added 4K Omarchy wordmark wallpapers (`01-omarchy.webp`) for **[`last-horizon`](https://github.com/containerscrew/omarchy-last-horizon-theme)**, **[`solitude`](https://github.com/containerscrew/omarchy-solitude-theme)**, and **[`starship`](https://github.com/vyrx-dev/omarchy-starship-theme)**, so all **26 bundled MIT themes** include at least one 100%-MIT 4K wallpaper.
   - **`Sync PC wallpaper` Toggle (off by default):** Pairing or syncing with a PC never overwrites the TV's bundled 4K MIT wallpaper unless you explicitly enable *Sync PC wallpaper* in the TV's Themes or Wallpaper menu.
3. **Native MCP Server (TV `POST /mcp` & PC `omarchy-tv mcp`):**
   - Control your TV from **Grok Bot**, **Claude Desktop**, **Cursor**, **Hermes**, or any Model Context Protocol (`2024-11-05`, JSON-RPC 2.0) client using a strict TV-only tool whitelist (`tv_get_status`, `tv_list_themes`, `tv_set_theme`, `tv_send_key`, `tv_launch_app`, `tv_cast_media`, `tv_show_notification`, `tv_open_ai_webapp`).
4. **Screensaver Effect Speed (`Slow / Normal / Fast`):**
   - Adjust the animation speed for all 37 `tte.js` effects and the native ASCII fallback from the Screensaver menu or via the Grok Bot TUI (`speed slow`, `speed normal`, `speed fast`).
5. **Multi-Brand Live TV & Menu Fixes (Community Feedback):**
   - Native **Sharp AQUOS** (`jp.co.sharp.av.android.aquostvapp`) and multi-brand Live TV detection alongside Sony BRAVIA (`com.sony.dtv.tvx`), Google TV (`com.google.android.tv`), TCL, Hisense, and Philips.
   - Smooth D-pad scrolling across long menus (`Themes` menu scrolls smoothly through all 26 themes on 1080p TVs).
   - Fixed `Hide from launcher` on the Home shelf and app grid, and added a direct **Hidden apps** manager in Workspace 5 (`System`).

---

## Complete Feature Overview

### 1. Android TV Launcher (`com.omarchytv.home`)
- **Authentic Omarchy Desktop Look on TV**: Hyprland-style windows (`BoxView` 2 px borders with `btop`-style cut-out legends), Waybar-style top bar, Walker-style fuzzy search (`long OK` or `Search`), and `CaskaydiaMono` font.
- **Workspaces 1–5**: `1` Home, `2` TV & Inputs, `3` All Apps, `4` PC Link & AI, `5` System & Settings. Switch workspaces with number keys `1–5` or the top bar.
- **Native Grok Bot · Omarchy TUI (`AskActivity`)**: Built-in terminal assistant on the Home shelf supporting standalone local TV commands, voice recognition, paired PC CLI streaming, and 1-click launch of full AI WebApps (`Grok Web`, `Grok (X)`, `ChatGPT`, `Claude`, `Hermes`).
- **One-Press Live TV & HDMI Inputs**: Supports Sony BRAVIA, Sharp AQUOS, Google TV, AOSP TV, DTVKit, TCL, Hisense, Philips, and standard Android TV Input Framework (`TIF`) channels.
- **26 Bundled MIT Themes & 4K Wallpapers**: Instant live theme switching with bundled 4K WebP backgrounds, `"next wallpaper"` cycling, custom image support, procedural aurora fallback, and custom theme packs pushed from your PC.
- **Customizable Home Panels**: Toggle individual panels (Clock, Weather with `°C / °F` switch and auto-location, PC Stats, AI Credits, Deploys, Terminal) and move them on a **12×8 grid** with **Arrange panels**.
- **App Shelf & Hidden Apps Manager**: Reorder or pin favorite apps, hide unwanted system tiles (including optional Sony bloatware toggle), restore hidden tiles in Workspace 5 (`System → Hidden apps`), and push custom 16:9 PNG app banners (`omarchy-tv icons push`).
- **37 `tte.js` ASCII Screensaver Effects**: Runs all 37 `TerminalTextEffects` / `tte.js` animations in a dedicated `:saver` process with configurable idle timeout (`1 / 2.5 / 5 / 10 min` or `Never`), **Effect speed (`Slow / Normal / Fast`)**, native fallback for legacy WebViews, and Android Daydream (`OmarchyDream`) support.
- **Cast to TV (opt-in)**: Send videos, audio (Media3 ExoPlayer), images, text, and links from your paired PC/Mac directly to the TV.
- **Crash Watchdog & Safe Debloat**: Independent `:watchdog` process that restores the stock launcher if 3 crashes ever occur within 5 minutes; safe debloat scripts use only reversible `pm disable-user --user 0` (never `pm uninstall`, never touching DNS or `setupwraith`).

### 2. PC / macOS Plugin (`omarchy-tv` + `omarchy-link`) — [pc-plugin/](pc-plugin/README.md)
- **SPAKE2 Encrypted Pairing**: Pair with a 6-digit code shown on the TV; all requests are signed with per-PC `OTV1` HMAC-SHA256 tokens over LAN.
- **Live PC Telemetry**: Pushes CPU, RAM, active media player (`playerctl`), and deploy status every 5 seconds only while the TV Home screen is visible.
- **Theme Sync & Custom Theme Push**: Syncs your active Omarchy desktop theme to the TV (`omarchy-tv themes push` uploads custom themes & 4K wallpapers, up to 50 MB total on TV).
- **Zero-API-Cost AI CLI Bridge**: Answers prompts from the TV's **Grok Bot · Omarchy TUI** using your already-signed-in desktop CLIs (`grok`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `hermes`, or local `ollama`).
- **Native MCP Server (`omarchy-tv mcp`)**: Exposes your TV to desktop AI agents over stdio (`--stdio`) or localhost HTTP (`--http --port 8990`, bound to `127.0.0.1` with a 256-bit Bearer token in `~/.config/omarchy-tv/mcp-token`).
- **Low-Latency H.264 Desktop Screen Mirroring ("PC Screen")**: Streams your Linux desktop to the TV via `gpu-screen-recorder` or `wf-recorder`.
- **Wireless Updater (`omarchy-tv update`)**: Updates Android TV via `adb` (verifying signing certificate and versionCode) and LG webOS via `ares-install`.

### 3. Android Smartphone Companion (`OmarchyTV Mobile`, `178 KB`) — [mobile-companion/](mobile-companion/README-MOBILE.md)
- **No-PC Wireless TV Installer**: Scans your `/24` Wi-Fi LAN, downloads the latest release from GitLab/GitHub, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, performs a pure-Java 2048-bit RSA Wireless ADB handshake (`:5555`), installs OmarchyTV (`pm install -r`), and pins it as your default Home launcher in one tap.
- **Live Theme Switcher & Touch Remote**: Switch all **26 MIT themes** in real time, control the TV with a tactile D-Pad and media keys, upload custom phone photos as TV wallpapers, and run safe 1-tap reversible brand debloat (`pm disable-user --user 0` / `pm enable`).
- **LG webOS & Universal Smart TV Bridge (`:8765`)**: Serves themes/wallpapers to LG webOS TVs and hosts the full 1080p HTML5 OmarchyTV Web Launcher (`http://<phone-ip>:8765/tv`) for **Samsung Tizen** and **Hisense VIDAA** TVs.

---

Every theme bundled in OmarchyTV `2.12.0-beta` is **100% MIT-licensed** and ships inside the APK with its palette (`assets/omarchy_themes.json`) and verified 4K WebP wallpapers (`assets/wallpapers/<theme>/`). ## Installation & Usage Guide

### 1. Install on Android TV / Google TV / Sony BRAVIA / Sharp AQUOS (`2.12.0-beta`)

#### Option A — Install via ADB from a PC / Mac
1. On your TV, enable Developer Options: **Settings → Device Preferences → About → press Build 7 times**, then enable **USB debugging / Network debugging** in **Developer options** and note the TV's IP address.
2. Connect and install the signed release APK:
   ```bash
   adb connect <tv-ip>:5555
   sha256sum omarchytv-release-2.12.0-beta.apk
   # Expected SHA-256: 9dedc335fb1150afa6027f4123bd295bec8241a4c654842a6be65caff993f035
   apksigner verify --print-certs omarchytv-release-2.12.0-beta.apk
   # Expected Signer #1 SHA-256: 90aa68d9f45e623eadfd349ab1eb66042356f95ff6347a4568c3f3a78f8ea33d
   adb install -r omarchytv-release-2.12.0-beta.apk
   ```
3. **Set OmarchyTV as the default Home screen (optional):**
   ```bash
   adb shell cmd package set-home-activity --user 0 com.omarchytv.home/.MainActivity
   ```
4. **Set OmarchyTV as the system screensaver (optional):**
   ```bash
   adb shell settings put secure screensaver_components com.omarchytv.home/.OmarchyDream
   adb shell settings put secure screensaver_enabled 1
   ```

#### Option B — Install Wirelessly from Your Android Smartphone (`OmarchyTV Mobile`, no PC needed)
1. Install **`omarchytv-mobile-2.12.0-beta.apk`** (`178 KB`, SHA-256: `42bb62aa6169c52afacc9b477d25f6f95fffe2eeea9f779394606e1a4e5ad0a4`) on your Android phone.
2. Tap **Scan LAN** to auto-discover your TV on `:5555` / `:47800`.
3. Tap **1-Tap Install / Update OmarchyTV** — the phone downloads the release APK, verifies the SHA-256 digest, performs a 2048-bit RSA Wireless ADB handshake, installs the APK via `pm install -r`, and pins OmarchyTV as your Home screen.

Full step-by-step guide: **[launcher/docs/INSTALL.md](launcher/docs/INSTALL.md)** · Safe debloat: **[docs/DEBLOAT.md](docs/DEBLOAT.md)** · AI-assisted setup: **[docs/AI-ASSISTED-SETUP.md](docs/AI-ASSISTED-SETUP.md)**.

### 2. Using the TV Launcher & Remote Controls

- **Switch Workspaces (`1–5`)**: Press number keys `1`–`5` on your remote, or press **▲ Up** to focus the top Waybar and select `1` (Home), `2` (TV & HDMI Inputs), `3` (All Apps), `4` (PC Link & AI), or `5` (System & Settings).
- **Open the Main Omarchy Menu**: Click the `[ ☰ ]` icon on the top-left of the Waybar, or press the **MENU** key on your remote.
- **Open Walker Fuzzy Search**: Long-press **OK / Center** on the Home screen (or press the Search key) to search apps, themes, settings, and AI commands (`> grok bot`, `> ask`).
- **Switch Themes & 4K Wallpapers**: Open **Menu → Themes** (scrolls smoothly through all 26 MIT themes with D-pad ▲/▼) or **Menu → Wallpaper → Next background** (`Sync PC wallpaper` is off by default so your TV's bundled 4K MIT wallpapers are preserved).
- **Customize App Tiles & Hidden Apps**: Long-press **OK** (or press **MENU**) on any app tile to move it, pin/unpin it from the Home row, or select **Hide from launcher**. To unhide any app later, open **Workspace 5 (`System`) → Hidden apps**.

### 3. Using the Native Grok Bot · Omarchy TUI on Your TV

Click the **Grok Bot** tile (`grokbot@tv:~$ > GROK BOT [ omarchy · tui ]`) on the Home shelf — or open **Menu → Grok Bot & AI → Grok Bot (Omarchy TUI)** — to launch the native Omarchy terminal assistant.

You can interact using the **1-click D-pad quick-action chips** at the top of the window, your **TV voice remote (`[ 🎤 voice ]`)**, or the **`grokbot@omarchytv:~$` command prompt**:

| Command / Action | What It Does (Works Offline on the TV!) |
|---|---|
| `theme <name>` (e.g. `theme jade-horse`, `theme year-of-the-horse`, `theme hermarchy`) | Immediately switches the active Omarchy theme and loads its bundled 4K MIT wallpaper |
| `next theme` / `[ ⏭ next theme ]` / `[ 🎨 themes ▾ ]` | Cycles to the next MIT theme or opens the 26-theme popup selector |
| `themes` | Lists all 26 bundled MIT themes in the terminal transcript |
| `wallpaper` / `next wallpaper` / `[ 🖼 wallpaper ]` | Cycles through the bundled 4K wallpapers for the current theme |
| `screensaver` / `[ ✦ screensaver ]` | Starts the 37-effect `tte.js` ASCII screensaver immediately |
| `speed slow` · `speed normal` · `speed fast` | Sets the screensaver animation speed |
| `open <app>` (e.g. `open YouTube`, `open Netflix`, `open TV`) | Launches any installed Android TV app by name or opens Live TV |
| `apps` / `[ 📦 apps ]` | Lists all installed TV apps in the terminal window |
| `status` / `mcp` / `[ 📊 status ]` | Displays TV hardware, Android/SDK version, active theme/wallpaper, and the TV MCP endpoint (`http://<tv-ip>:47800/mcp`) |
| `web` / `grok.com` / `chatgpt` / `claude` / `hermes` / `[ 🌐 grok.com ]` / `[ 🌐 web ▾ ]` | Opens the full browser WebApp in the isolated `:web` process (`WebAppActivity`) with persistent login and D-pad cursor |
| *Any open-ended question* (when paired with a PC via `omarchy-link`) | Streams the answer from your PC's authenticated AI CLI (`grok`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `hermes`, `ollama`) with optional TTS readout |

```bash
tar -xzf omarchy-tv-pc-plugin-2.12.0-beta.tar.gz

omarchy-tv

# Start the MCP server for Grok Bot / Claude Desktop / Cursor / Hermes:
omarchy-tv mcp --stdio                 # stdio MCP mode (JSON-RPC 2.0, protocolVersion 2024-11-05)
omarchy-tv mcp --http --port 8990      # HTTP MCP mode (127.0.0.1:8990, token in ~/.config/omarchy-tv/mcp-token)
```

- **Works**: Android TV and Google TV devices (Android 7+). Tested on Sony KD-55XE9005 (Android 9), Google TV Streamer (Android 14), Sharp AQUOS, and Noblex/Hisense (Android 11). Needs network debugging / adb.

- **Untested**: Fire OS devices (Fire TV Stick 4K Max / 4K Plus, Android-based) and projectors with Android TV (e.g. JMGO global versions).
- **Not supported natively**: Fire TV Stick 4K Select (Amazon Vega OS, not Android), Roku, Apple TV.
